title: Redwood Console - Tracing & Request Logs Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE did a console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for payments workloads; security and audit logs are primary concerns. Team requested pricing for a dedicated pilot, security docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS), and a short benchmarking run on their error-heavy flows. Agreed next step: send pricing + security pack, schedule a 2-hour deep-dive with infra team, and provide a sample trace/export for their failing transaction set.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated / Private deployment tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Start: 15:23 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah (Redwood); James Rhee, Maya Lopez, Sana Rahman, Evan Torres (Acme)
Notes: call recorded, auto-transcript (medium quality)

Summary/Intended agenda: quick console walkthrough — tracing, error analysis, request logs — then Q&A about security/hosting options and next steps.

[00:00] Alex Kim: great, hi everyone this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the account lead, thanks for joining. priya is here from our solutions eng team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] James Rhee: hey, doing good. thanks for setting this up. we wanted to see how the console helps us debug high error rates in our payments flows — we've seen intermittent 5xx spikes during settlement windows.
[00:18] Priya Shah: yeah hi i'm priya. i'll walk through the tracing view, the request logs, and a couple of debugging flows — show how we'd triage a failing transaction. apologies in advance if the auto-transcript gets names weird, the system sometimes turns KV cache into K V cash, so ignore that.
[00:32] Maya Lopez: ha ok noted.
[00:34] Alex Kim: quick run of context — acme is evaluating a pilot, right? you're leaning towards dedicated/reserved capacity because of throughput and residency, but want to see how debugging and observability works before committing. is that the gist?
[00:46] James Rhee: yes. security is big for us — SOC2, encryption, KMS integration, audit logs. and latency/cost tradeoffs. we want to make sure we can reproduce issues with traces and that logs are detailed enough.
[00:58] Priya Shah: perfect, i'll jump into the console share. you can see i'm in the Traces tab; on the left is the runbook for error analysis, and middle is a waterfall view for individual requests.
[01:15] Priya Shah: (screen) here's a recent failing transaction — you'll notice the root call shows a tokenization step that took longer, then a spike in retries. the waterfall lets you expand spans; span names come from model call boundaries and middleware. sometimes our auto-parse mislabels a span if the model name is unusual, that's expected.
[01:38] Evan Torres: can you filter by model version? sometimes we pin a smaller quantized variant in staging.
[01:42] Priya Shah: yep, top filter lets you narrow by model, model_version, and by policy (hosted vs dedicated). you can also group by route, which helps if you have multiple prompt templates.
[01:55] Sana Rahman: is PII masked in these traces by default? we can't have raw card numbers in logs.
[02:02] Priya Shah: good question — by default we redact common PII patterns, and there are config flags for stricter scrubbing. for Private deployments you can plug-in your own scrubbing pipeline. we'll include the docs and the how-to video for that.
[02:18] James Rhee: any chance we can see the underlying request logs for that trace? want to see headers and metadata.
[02:23] Priya Shah: yes, if you click Request Details -> Request Logs it shows a time-series and raw-ish request rows. we store request-level metadata (route, model, latency, cost, status, customer_meta) and you can export CSV or JSON for a subset.
[02:39] Priya Shah: (screen) here is a quick filter: status:500, model:gpt-like-4q, last_24h — you can pipeline that into a saved-view and set an alert.
[02:53] Maya Lopez: the saved views look nice. how long are logs retained in hosted by default?
[02:58] Alex Kim: for hosted default retention is 30 days, with longer retention add-ons — we also offer enterprise retention options for Dedicated/Private, we can map retention to your compliance needs.
[03:10] James Rhee: ok, that's fine but we'll need at least 90 days of request logs for audit trails.
[03:16] Alex Kim: understood — we'll put that in the security pack.
[03:19] Priya Shah: back to tracing — you can click an error span to see the stack and the request payload sample. sometimes the transcript generation makes the stack look odd — e.g., shows 'sam-el' for SAML — but the raw JSON export is accurate.
[03:36] Evan Torres: can we correlate traces to our internal request IDs? we tag inbound requests with x-acme-trace-id.
[03:42] Priya Shah: yes, you can map custom headers; there's a routing header mapping page in settings. we ingest and index custom ids for correlation.
[03:50] James Rhee: nice. about debugging flows — suppose we see 10% increased latency during peak, what's the triage path?
[04:00] Priya Shah: the console has a diagnostic runbook: first, check per-route P50/P95, then look at model-level hot spots, then prefix-KV cache hit rates — the KPI charts show cache hit ratio; if KV cache drop correlates with increased latency we can look at the autoscaling events.
[04:20] Priya Shah: note, sometimes the auto-transcript will flip KV cache to "K V cash" which is wrong, but the UI shows the metric nicely.
[04:28] Maya Lopez: you mentioned autoscaling events — can we see those logs tied to traces?
[04:33] Priya Shah: yes, Autoscales show as system events; there's a timeline overlay on the trace waterfall so you can see scaling and routing fallbacks inline.
[04:44] James Rhee: ok, what about rollbacks or automatic fallback to smaller models during capacity pressure? will that show up in traces?
[04:52] Priya Shah: it will — the span will include the actual model executed and a note if it was a fallback variant. you can also set alert policies to notify on fallbacks.
[05:03] (short pause / screen scroll)
[05:10] Priya Shah: moving to Error Analysis tab. here we group by error signature; top groups are timeouts and malformed responses. you can click into a group to see sample request rows and a histogram by route.
[05:25] Alex Kim: this is often where customers find systemic issues — e.g., prompt templates that sometimes return bad JSON and cause downstream parsers to crash.
[05:34] James Rhee: can the console run quick replays of requests against a test model to reproduce?
[05:39] Priya Shah: yes, we have a Replay feature — you can replay a request against a pinned model version or a local test endpoint. it's subject to rate limits in hosted but very handy for reproducing.
[05:52] Evan Torres: is replaying safe for PII? we need to scrub before replay.
[05:56] Priya Shah: replays can apply the same scrubbing rules or use a test-only scrubber. for Private deployments you can set replay to only work on anonymized payloads.
[06:07] (crosstalk)
[06:09] Sana Rahman: on audit logs — do you provide immutable audit for admin actions? our compliance team wants to see who exported logs and who changed RBAC.
[06:18] Alex Kim: yes, we provide an Audit Log feed separate from request logs; entries include actor, action, resource, timestamp, and there's a tamper-evident hash if you need chain-of-custody. we'll include a sample audit log export in the security packet.
[06:33] Sana Rahman: perfect. encryption at rest — KMS? HSM?
[06:38] Priya Shah: supported. hosted customers use our managed KMS, Dedicated/Private can integrate with customer-managed KMS or HSM. Key wrapping and envelope encryption are supported.
[06:48] James Rhee: can you show the request logs view quickly?
[06:52] Priya Shah: sure. (screen) Request Logs tab — searchable rows with columns: timestamp, route, model, latency_ms, status, cost_tokens, trace_id, customer_id. filters at top for time range, status, model, route, cost.
[07:12] Priya Shah: you can save the filter as a saved-view and pin it to the dashboard. downstream, alerts can trigger on saved-view thresholds.
[07:22] Maya Lopez: does the logs table support text search inside prompt or response snippets?
[07:27] Priya Shah: yes with limitations — we index snippets (first 2k chars) and offer substring search; full-text search on responses is available as an add-on.
[07:36] James Rhee: about exporting — can we bulk export the last 30 days of errors for our compliance review? CSV/JSON?
[07:43] Priya Shah: CSV and JSON exports are available; for large exports we provide an S3 dump for Dedicated/Private or an export job in hosted that places file in your cloud storage.
[07:55] Alex Kim: i want to flag that exports with sensitive fields should be scrubbed — we'll include instructions to use our scrubbing pipeline during export.
[08:04] (short silence)
[08:09] James Rhee: one operational question — we run on GCP primarily, is there a region parity for your hosted service?
[08:16] Alex Kim: yes, we have hosted regions in us-east, europe-west, and ap-southeast — Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions or on-prem. we'll confirm exact GCP region parity in follow-up.
[08:30] Evan Torres: let's talk about an example — we sent a sample failing transaction earlier in the thread. can Priya show how she'd triage that with traces?
[08:40] Priya Shah: sure — i'm uploading the sample trace now (demo-only). here you see multiple retries on tokenization with spikes in latency and increased error rate. the trace shows a third-party transform timing out.
[08:53] Priya Shah: expand the span, in the details you can see headers, the request payload sample (redacted), and the error message. sometimes the auto-transcript will mangle acronyms — e.g., SAML becomes "sam el" — but the error text is the original.
[09:07] Maya Lopez: if the problem's in a third-party transform, can we annotate the trace or attach issue IDs?
[09:12] Priya Shah: yes, you can add annotations and link an external ticket (Jira/GitHub). annotations flow into the trace metadata and are visible to teammates.
[09:21] James Rhee: and RBAC — who can see these traces? we need to limit to infra and security.
[09:26] Alex Kim: RBAC is per-feature. you can grant trace-viewing to roles; audit logs will capture exports and view events. we'll include an RBAC example policy.
[09:37] (screen scroll)
[09:40] Priya Shah: quick note on performance — tracing has low overhead in the runtime; we snapshot minimal payload metadata by default and capture full request payload only when you mark a request for deep-dive or if sampling rules match. that keeps costs down.
[09:58] Evan Torres: what's the sampling strategy? p99 capture?
[10:02] Priya Shah: default is adaptive sampling: capture all errors, and sample successful requests by rate + weight by latency (more likely to capture slow requests). you can customize sampling rules in settings.
[10:15] James Rhee: cost — does tracing add per-token costs?
[10:19] Alex Kim: tracing itself incurs minimal request-metadata storage cost; we also show cost-by-request in the UI. heavy capture of full payloads or long retention will increase storage/ingest fees. we'll show cost examples in the pricing pack.
[10:32] (brief pause)
[10:36] Priya Shah: moving to debugging flows — i'll demo a quick reproduce: filter failures by route, replay two samples against a pinned model and reproduce the malformed response. then open an inline debugger that shows model outputs and the post-processing stage; you can step through sanitization and see where parsing fails.
[10:58] Maya Lopez: that step-through debugger looks useful. can we run it in a sandbox that uses our test keys?
[11:04] Priya Shah: yes, sandboxes can be configured with test credentials and test model variants.
[11:11] James Rhee: will the debugger surface tokenization issues? we've had cases where whitespace or unicode breaks tokenization.
[11:18] Priya Shah: it will — tokenizer breakpoints and token-level view are part of the debug flow; you can export tokenization maps. sometimes transcripts show odd words, e.g., 'token 0' as 'token zero' but the binary export is accurate.
[11:32] Evan Torres: curious about tracing across multiple services — our flow touches a Java microservice then a node worker then the model. can Redwood traces join those spans?
[11:40] Priya Shah: we support trace context propagation via standard headers (W3C traceparent or custom). you can push Redwood trace_id into your service traces to join them, or ingest external trace IDs.
[11:50] James Rhee: sweet. any gotchas for private deployments?
[11:54] Priya Shah: in Private you manage the control plane and can keep logs in customer storage; we also support offline exporters for air-gapped environments. some features like Hosted-managed replay are limited in air-gapped modes but we provide local tooling.
[12:09] Sana Rahman: regarding compliance, will you sign an SOC2 + data processing addendum?
[12:14] Alex Kim: yes, standard — we'll include the DPA and SOC2 summary; for enterprise accounts we can do data residency and custom contractual terms.
[12:24] (screen scrolling / small talk)
[12:30] Priya Shah: one last bit: request logs have link-throughs to traces so you can jump from a log row into the full waterfall; we also have an error regression tool that surfaces quality regressions tied to prompt sets and eval suites.
[12:49] James Rhee: that regression tool could be useful for our weekly QA. how does it detect regressions?
[12:54] Priya Shah: it compares eval outputs across model versions and prompt sets, flags divergence and can tie failures back to traces when available.
[13:05] Maya Lopez: ok, vendor comparison — James: is Acme considering other providers?
[13:09] James Rhee: yes we're also looking at OpenAI's tooling and Vertex AI.
[13:14] Alex Kim: understood. our differentiators are production-first tracing and unified controls across hosted/dedicated/private, plus cost controls like KV cache and batching suggestions in Optimize.
[13:26] (short silence)
[13:30] Alex Kim: looks like we're around 13 minutes in, but we planned a 45 minute session — do you want to keep going into deeper debug or switch to Q&A?
[13:38] James Rhee: let's keep going for a bit, priya can you show how alerts are configured for trace-derived signals?
[13:44] Priya Shah: sure — Alerts page; you can create alert on saved-view thresholds, e.g., >5% error rate or >200ms p95 for a route. alerts can push to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. we also show outbreak detection that correlates routes with infra events.
[14:04] Maya Lopez: which team owns the alerting config in a Dedicated setup — customer or Redwood?
[14:09] Alex Kim: ownership is flexible — by default the customer manages alerts, but Redwood can manage on-call and config under a managed services add-on.
[14:19] Evan Torres: back to request ids — if we want to stream logs into our SIEM, is there a connector?
[14:25] Priya Shah: yes we have native connectors for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic and a generic S3/HTTP export. for Dedicated/Private we'd usually provide a direct shipper.
[14:36] (brief pause)
[14:40] James Rhee: a couple of remaining security questions: do you support SSO and SCIM for user provisioning?
[14:46] Alex Kim: yes SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for provisioning; we'll include setup instructions in the packet.
[14:55] Sana Rahman: how do you handle data deletion requests? we need to support deletion within certain windows.
[15:01] Priya Shah: we have deletion APIs and a manual purge process; for hosted we guarantee deletion within X days per contract, for Private you control retention. we'll include the DPA excerpt.
[15:13] (screen scroll, short aside)
[15:18] Priya Shah: demo wrap-up: saved views, trace waterfall, request logs, replay, annotation, audit logs, export.
[15:25] James Rhee: solid. can you send an example of the trace export from today's sample? i want to hand it to our infra folks.
[15:31] Alex Kim: will do — priya, can you generate a sample trace export and attach?
[15:35] Priya Shah: yes i'll generate a redacted JSON export and share the link — note it will have tokenization maps and span metadata. i'll scrub PII before sending.
[15:44] Maya Lopez: please also include instructions to enable stricter scrubbing.
[15:49] Alex Kim: quick recap of next steps: i'll send pricing and the security packet by Monday 6/15; priya will send the how-to + sample export; evan will send anonymized failing transactions; and we'll set up a deeper infra session week of 6/22.
[15:59] James Rhee: sounds good. any blockers on our side?
[16:02] Maya Lopez: none, just need to check internal calendars.
[16:05] Sana Rahman: can you include a short data flow diagram in the packet showing where logs and traces live and who can access them?
[16:11] Alex Kim: will include that.
[16:14] (closing)
[16:15] Alex Kim: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and the packet.
[16:19] James Rhee: thanks all.
[16:22] (call ends)

Post-call notes (auto): transcript has occasional mis-attributions and transcription errors (e.g., KV cache spelled K V cash; SAML spoken as sam el). Saved recording and export: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20260612-1523-acme-console-walkthrough (demo link, redacted). Relevant docs linked during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/console/tracing, https://redwood.ai/docs/security/soc2-dpa, shared drive link to sample export (redacted).

End of transcript.
